description: A clock, LFO, sample and hold and noise source in one, after the RVG cell in Warren Burt's Aardvark IV. A simulated R-2R converter of 1 to 10 bits picks values out of 10V

params.text: How much of the voltage at the CLK FM input moves the clock rate
How much of the voltage at the offset CV input reaches the offset
How much of the voltage at the portamento CV input reaches the portamento
How much of the voltage at the gain CV input reaches the gain
The threshold the stepped value is measured against, 0.01V to 9.99V, default 5.00V

inputs.text: A clock here takes over from the internal clock and is copied to the clock outputs, so several of these can be run from one clock
A voltage moving the clock rate
A voltage moving the offset added to the stepped and smooth outputs, read up to 15V either way
A voltage moving the gain, 1.00x per 5V and clamped to -2.00x and +2.00x

outputs.text: A 1ms pulse at the clock rate
A square wave at the clock rate, high for half of each cycle
A ramp rising over each clock cycle
A ramp falling over each clock cycle
The value picked by the converter, multiplied by the gain with the offset added
The stepped value with portamento applied to it
Sends a 1ms pulse each time the clock arrives while the stepped value is above the comparator threshold
Sends a pulse when the clock is resynced, for passing the sync on to another of these

notes: a red display is set by dragging it, and the further left the drag starts the faster the value moves; the green display beside one shows the value actually in use once modulation is added
the clock runs from 0.01Hz to 8kHz, default 10.00Hz, and aliases badly above about 20Hz, so it suits modulation rather than audio
the offset display runs from -15V to +15V, default 0.00V, and the gain display from -2.00x to +2.00x, default 1.00x
BITS sets the resolution of the converter from 1 to 10 bits and NUM VALUES shows how many values that gives, from 2 to 1024
DEV % sets the tolerance of the resistors in the simulated converter, 0 to 20 percent, default 2 percent; the tolerances are worked out again each time it is changed
portamento runs from 0.00 to 1.00, default 0.50, and acts only on the smooth output; settings above 0.90 slow it a great deal
a clock patched into the clock input takes over from the internal clock and is copied to the clock outputs, so several of these can be chained from one clock
the sync output passes a resync on in the same way as the clock outputs pass the clock on
